records.question: How many credits do I need to take to be full-time as a graduate student?
search_queries: How many credits do I need to take to be full-time as a graduate student?
records.answer:
As an F-1 or J-1 graduate student, you need to register for **at least 9 credits each term** to be considered full-time.

Key conditions:
- **Online courses:** No more than 3 credits of online/distance coursework can count toward your full-time minimum. That means at least 6 of your credits must be face-to-face or hybrid.
- **Audited courses** don't count toward the full-time minimum.
- **Less than full time:** If you can't register for 9 credits, you must get written permission from ISSS *before* the term begins (or before dropping below full-time). LTFT requests need your academic advisor's approval and must be submitted by the add/drop deadline, or at the latest before the withdrawal deadline (Friday of week 7). Without authorization, you're considered out of immigration status.
- **Dropping or withdrawing** from a course mid-semester requires approval from an ISSS advisor first.

If you're thinking of reducing your course load, please talk to an ISSS advisor before making any changes.

records.question: How many online credits can count toward my full-time enrollment each term?
search_queries: How many online credits can count toward my full-time enrollment each term?
records.answer:

- That means undergraduates need at least 9 credits, and graduate students at least 6 credits, in face-to-face or hybrid classes each term (on top of the 3 online credits, to reach 12 or 9 total).

Don't drop or withdraw from a course without first getting approval from an ISSS advisor. If you need to go below full-time, you must get written permission from ISSS before the term begins (or follow the LTFT process described on the ISSS page).

records.question: How many hours a week can I work on campus while classes are in session?
search_queries: How many hours a week can I work on campus while classes are in session?
records.answer:
You can work **no more than 20 hours per week** on campus while school is in session. F-1 and J-1 students can work more than 20 hours only during an approved vacation term, and you should check Human Resources' own policies for that period.

Key conditions:
- You must be maintaining valid F-1/J-1 status, and your I-20/DS-2019 must not have expired. You also must not have graduated.
- If you're on co-op, your co-op job counts as your "class," so on-campus work is still limited to 20 hours per week. ISSS strongly discourages doing both at the same time.
- J-1 students need prior ISSS authorization for any on-campus job.
- On-campus work must not hurt your academic performance. Failing or dropping classes can affect your full-time enrollment and may lead to termination of your SEVIS record.

For your specific situation, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
search_queries: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
records.answer:
F-1 students have a **60-day grace period** after their program ends. The same 60 days applies after Post-Completion OPT ends, but only if you completed your OPT. Students who exceeded the 90-day unemployment limit aren't eligible for it.

**During the grace period you may:**
- Prepare to leave the U.S. and travel within the U.S.
- Arrange to transfer or start a new program, change status, or depart.

You may **not** work or study during this time. If you leave the U.S. before the grace period ends, you can't re-enter on your F-1 status after your I-20 expiration date.

**If you apply for OPT:** USCIS must receive your application before your 60 days end. Your F-1 status then stays active until USCIS decides, even if more than 60 days pass.

**Possible future change:** ISSS announcements describe a DHS proposal (2025) and a final rule on duration of status (published July 2026) that would reduce the F-1 grace period to 30 days. A US District Court postponed that rule's effective date (announcement of September 14, 2026), and I don't have details on its current status. The ISSS pages on maintaining status and OPT still say 60 days. Please confirm with an ISSS advisor before relying on a date.

records.question: How much OPT can I get?
search_queries: How much OPT can I get?
records.answer:
**Standard OPT:** F-1 students get a total of 12 months of OPT for each degree level (Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate). You can use some of it during your program (Pre-Completion OPT) or save all 12 months for after graduation (Post-Completion OPT).
- Pre-completion full-time OPT counts at 100% (6 months used = 6 months deducted).
- Pre-completion part-time OPT counts at 50% (6 months used = 3 months deducted).

**STEM OPT Extension:** If you're in a STEM field and meet the criteria, you may be eligible for an additional 24 months of Post-Completion OPT. You can't request all 36 months at once. You must first apply for the initial 12 months of Post-Completion OPT, then apply for the extension while your OPT EAD card is still active.

**Proposed change:** On October 9, 2026, ISSS announced that DHS proposed a rule that would require universities to pay a $70,000 fee per OPT authorization and $30,000 for subsequent STEM OPT requests. ISSS says this has no immediate impact, and current OPT and STEM OPT processes remain unchanged unless DHS finalizes and implements the rule.

To confirm your own eligibility, check with an ISSS advisor (isss@drexel.edu).

records.question: How many days can I be unemployed on post-completion OPT?
search_queries: How many days can I be unemployed on post-completion OPT?
records.answer:
You can be unemployed for a maximum of **90 days** in total (aggregate) during Post-Completion OPT. Every day counts, including weekends, from the employment start date shown on your EAD card until you have qualifying employment.

Key points:
- **Reporting:** If you exceed 90 days or don't follow the OPT reporting requirements, it is a violation of F-1 status. Your SEVIS record may be terminated.
- **Before you hit the limit:** The ISSS page says you should prepare to transfer to another SEVP-certified school, change educational level, leave the U.S., or otherwise act to maintain status.
- **Grace period:** Students who exceed the 90-day unemployment limit are not eligible for the 60-day grace period.
- **Work hours:** Post-Completion OPT work must be at least 20 hours per week. Contact ISSS if you have concerns about meeting this.
- **STEM OPT:** If you are approved for a 24-month STEM extension, you get an additional 60 unemployment days, for a maximum of 150 days in total. You must report any job loss to ISSS.

If you're close to the limit or unsure how your days are counted, please confirm with your ISSS advisor.

records.question: Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?
search_queries: Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?
records.answer:
No, you don't need a job offer to apply for OPT. The ISSS OPT page says a job offer is not required to apply.

Some conditions apply after you're approved:

- **Post-Completion OPT:** You're expected to actively look for work in your field and be employed for at least nine months after your OPT start date (as shown on your EAD). There is an aggregate limit of 90 days of "unemployment" while on Post-Completion OPT. Every day without qualifying employment counts, including weekends, starting from the start date on your EAD.
- **Pre-Completion OPT:** There is no penalty for not working, but any time you don't work still counts against your 12 months of OPT eligibility.
- **Don't start work early:** You can't begin working until you have your EAD card and the OPT start date on it has arrived.

The 24-month STEM OPT extension is different. It requires a job or job offer directly related to your STEM degree, from an E-Verify employer.

Also, a recent announcement (October 9, 2026) says DHS has proposed new fees for OPT and STEM OPT. records.question: Can I be self-employed during the STEM OPT extension?
search_queries: Can I be self-employed during the STEM OPT extension?
records.answer:
No. According to ISSS, self-employment is not eligible for a STEM OPT extension. The regulations require a bona fide employer-employee relationship with an employer, so you can't be self-employed and can't provide employer attestations on your own behalf.

- **Start-ups:** You can be employed by a start-up business, as long as all regulatory requirements are met. You still can't attest on your own behalf.
- **Other STEM OPT employer requirements:** The employer must have an EIN, use E-Verify at your worksite, and offer work directly related to your qualifying STEM degree.
- **Unpaid or volunteer work:** This can't be the basis for a STEM OPT extension either.

**Standard OPT is different.** ISSS says students on regular (initial) OPT may be self-employed business owners, working full-time and able to prove proper business licenses and active engagement in a business related to their degree. That flexibility doesn't carry over to the STEM extension.

Since this affects your status, I recommend confirming your specific situation with an ISSS advisor before making plans.

records.question: Does my employer need to use E-Verify for my STEM OPT?

- **Other employer requirements:** The employer also needs an EIN and an employer-employee relationship with you, and the job must be directly related to your qualifying STEM degree.

If you're unsure whether your employer qualifies, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: How recent does the travel signature on my I-20 need to be when I come back to the U.S.?

- **Most F-1 students:** The [Travel Information page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/travel) says the travel signature must be issued within **12 months** of re-entry.

The December 2024 re-entry advisory only says "recent." The safer choice is to have a signature that is no more than 6 months old on your return date. Please confirm with ISSS.

**To request a signature:** Use the [Signature Request form](https://drexel.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KHlTvO1gmy8Sfs) from the re-entry advisory.

records.question: How much extra money do I need to show to bring my spouse and one child?
search_queries: How much extra money do I need to show to bring my spouse and one child?
records.answer:
The amount depends on your status.

This is in addition to the funds covering your tuition, fees, and living expenses, and it applies regardless of how long your dependents will stay in the U.S.

**J-1 scholar (J-2 DS-2019 request, a different page):** The J-1 scholars page lists **$600/month for a spouse and $400/month for each child**. For a spouse and one child, that is $1,000 per month. This page is about hiring-related J-1 scholars, so it probably doesn't apply if you are a student. If you aren't sure which category you are in, please confirm with ISSS.

**How to request:** Submit the Add a Dependent form on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx) with:
- A copy of each dependent's passport
- An updated official bank statement
- Proof of marriage (for your spouse)
- Proof of birth (for your child)

For the full details, see [Request For Dependent I-20/DS-2019](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/dependents) and [J1 Exchange Visitors](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/hiring-foreign-nationals/j1-scholars). records.question: I'm being held at the U.S. border on a Saturday night. Who do I call?

Call the ISSS after-hours emergency number: **215.629.6388**. This line is for immigration emergencies at the U.S. border outside normal business hours, including weekends, such as being denied entry or detained at the border for immigration reasons.

records.question: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?

records.answer:
Bachelor's and master's J-1 students are limited to **18 months** of Academic Training (AT), or the length of their degree program, whichever is shorter. Students pursuing a STEM degree may qualify for a special extension.

- AT during your studies and AT after your program ends are added together toward the limit, and full-time and part-time AT count equally.
- AT must be directly related to the major field on your DS-2019, and it must be approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date.

ISSS recommends submitting it at least three weeks in advance, since review takes about 4-5 business days.

**Possible upcoming change:** DHS published a final rule ending "duration of status" for F and J students, scheduled to take effect September 15, 2026. A later announcement (September 14, 2026) says a US District Court postponed that effective date. I don't have the details of that announcement, so please check it. Under the rule, J-1 students would need to apply to USCIS for an extension to do post-graduation AT.

records.question: What happens if I'm away from Drexel and not enrolled for more than five months?
search_queries: What happens if I'm away from Drexel and not enrolled for more than five months?
records.answer:
If you're not enrolled for more than five months, you'll need a **new I-20/DS-2019** and must **repay the SEVIS I-901 fee**. The same applies if your SEVIS record was terminated for reasons other than "Authorized Early Withdrawal."

**Key steps and conditions:**
- **Email ISSS at least 3 months before your planned return** to get instructions on applying for the new I-20/DS-2019.
- **Break in F-1 status:** Because of this absence, your F-1 status will be broken. After you return to the U.S., you must complete **at least one academic year of full-time study** before you're eligible for certain F-1 benefits, such as CPT or OPT.
- **Academic approval:** You must first get approval from your academic program to return from a leave of absence. Contact your academic advisor for how to report your return to Drexel.

**For comparison:** If your absence was authorized by ISSS and lasts less than five months, you can instead request SEVIS reactivation. This is subject to SEVP discretion, and if SEVP denies it, you'd need a new I-20.

Since this affects your immigration status, I recommend confirming your specific situation with an ISSS advisor before you leave. You can find contact details on the [ISSS website](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support).

records.question: Can I take less than a full course load in my final term?
search_queries: Can I take less than a full course load in my final term?
records.answer:
Yes, possibly. F-1 and J-1 students in the final term of their degree program can apply for less than full-time (LTFT) enrollment under "Completion of Studies" if the credits they still need to finish the program are fewer than what full-time enrollment requires.

**Conditions to know:**
- You can't take courses fully online in your final term. If you need more than one class to finish, you can count no more than one class (3 credits) of online study toward your remaining requirements.
- You must get ISSS authorization *before* you drop below full-time. Students who don't enroll full-time and lack LTFT approval are considered out of immigration status.

**How to apply:**
1. Complete the Less Than Full-Time form on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx?source=https%3a%2f%2fdrexel0.sharepoint.com%2fsites%2fISSS-StudentPortal%2fSitePages%2fForms%2fByAuthor.aspx).
2. Have your academic advisor specify the reason and sign it.
3. Email it to isss@drexel.edu, and wait for ISSS's approval decision.

**Deadline:** Submit by the add/drop deadline, or at the latest before the withdrawal deadline (Friday of week 7 of the term).

Also, if you're approved for a medical LTFT in your final term, you must still enroll in at least one course.

For advice on your specific situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: How old can my bank statement be for my I-20 application?

- Typed and in English

1. **Check eligibility.** You need to have been enrolled full-time and physically present in the U.S. for at least one full academic year (some graduate programs that require immediate CPT are an exception). 2. **Get curricular approval first.**

- You can't start CPT work before the official CPT start date.
- CPT is generally limited to 20 hours per week, with some exceptions (for example, full-time co-op).
- Non-co-op CPT is authorized term by term.
- CPT can't continue past your graduation date or I-20 end date.
- Full-time CPT for one year (364 days) or more eliminates OPT eligibility.

records.question: How do I apply for a reduced course load for medical reasons?
search_queries: How do I apply for a reduced course load for medical reasons?
records.answer:
To apply for a medical reduced course load (LTFT), get ISSS approval **before** you drop below full-time.

**Steps**
1. **Get a letter from your medical provider.** It must be on official letterhead and signed by a licensed medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, or licensed clinical psychologist. It should say you can't attend classes, or can't attend full-time, for a specific term. Your provider can use the template on the ISSS page. They don't have to give details about your diagnosis, but the letter must include everything the template requires. If you can't take any courses, the letter must say so clearly.
2. **Complete the Less Than Full-Time form** on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx?source=https%3a%2f%2fdrexel0.sharepoint.com%2fsites%2fISSS-StudentPortal%2fSitePages%2fForms%2fByAuthor.aspx). Your academic advisor must state the reason and sign it.
3. **Email the form and the doctor's letter together as one PDF** to isss@drexel.edu.
4. **Wait for ISSS's email decision** before dropping any courses.

**Key conditions**
- Submit by the add/drop deadline, or at the latest before the withdrawal deadline (Friday of week 7 of the term).
- ISSS must authorize medical LTFT for each term you request.
- Medical LTFT is limited to 12 aggregate months per program level.
- You're expected to return to full-time study when the LTFT period ends.
- If you're in your final term, you must enroll in at least one course under medical LTFT.

If you drop below full-time without authorization, you're considered out of immigration status. For questions about your own situation, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: What's the difference between CPT and OPT?
search_queries: What's the difference between CPT and OPT?
records.answer:
**CPT** and **OPT** are both F-1 off-campus work authorizations, but they differ in purpose and process.

**CPT (Curricular Practical Training)**
- It applies when an internship, co-op, practicum, or similar experience is a *required part of your specific academic program*. Work that is only beneficial or relevant doesn't qualify.
- ISSS reviews and authorizes it.
- Dates follow the official Drexel term dates, and authorization is term-by-term (except Steinbright-designated co-ops, which follow the co-op cycle).
- Using 364 days or more of full-time CPT eliminates your OPT eligibility. Part-time CPT and international co-op don't affect it.

**OPT (Optional Practical Training)**
- It lets you work in temporary employment directly related to your major and appropriate to your degree level. It's available before you complete your studies (Pre-Completion) and after (Post-Completion).
- You apply to USCIS, which can take 90 days or longer.
- To be eligible, you must have been a full-time student in the U.S. for at least one full academic year, be in lawful F-1 status, have fewer than 365 days of full-time CPT, and (for Post-Completion) have met your degree requirements.
- A job offer isn't required to apply, but during Post-Completion OPT you're expected to seek work in your field and be employed for at least nine months.

**Recent news:** On 2026-10-09, ISSS announced that DHS proposed new fees for OPT and STEM OPT. See the [announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/October/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Proposes-$70000-Fee-for-OPT-and-$30000-fee-for-STEM-OPT) for details.

For your own situation, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Can I work an on-campus job while I'm on co-op?
search_queries: Can I work an on-campus job while I'm on co-op?
records.answer:
Yes, but ISSS strongly discourages it. F-1 and J-1 students may work on campus while on co-op, but the conditions are strict:

- **20-hour limit:** During your co-op cycle, your co-op employment counts as your "class," so on-campus work is limited to 20 hours per week.
- **No impact on your co-op:** On-campus work must not interfere with your responsibilities at the co-op job.
- **Valid status:** You must be maintaining valid F-1/J-1 status, have an unexpired I-20/DS-2019, and not have graduated.
- **J-1 students:** You must get ISSS permission before starting any on-campus job. Email isss@drexel.edu with a copy of your job offer, including the position title and expected start and end dates.
- **F-1 students:** You don't need advance ISSS approval, but you'll need your documents ready for Drexel HR onboarding and the I-9.

The job must also count as "on-campus" (for example, employment by Drexel or an on-campus business like Aramark). If you're unsure whether a job qualifies, check with HR at hr@drexel.edu before accepting it.

If your co-op itself is in the U.S., it may need its own work authorization. The excerpts I have don't cover that, so please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Tôi có thể làm CPT trong năm học đầu tiên không?
search_queries: Tôi có thể làm CPT trong năm học đầu tiên không?
records.answer:
Nói chung là **không**. Theo ISSS, bạn phải đã học toàn thời gian trong chương trình cấp bằng và có mặt tại Mỹ ít nhất **một năm học đầy đủ** (3 quý hoặc 2 học kỳ) trước khi đủ điều kiện làm CPT.

**Ngoại lệ:** sinh viên cao học mà chương trình yêu cầu tham gia CPT ngay từ đầu.

**Các điều kiện khác của CPT:**
- Bạn có lời mời thực tập/đào tạo liên quan trực tiếp đến ngành học.
- Thực tập phải là yêu cầu bắt buộc để tốt nghiệp đối với tất cả sinh viên, bất kể tình trạng nhập cư. Chỉ vì công việc hữu ích hoặc có liên quan thì chưa đủ.
- Nếu có môn học đi kèm, bạn phải đăng ký môn đó trong học kỳ được cấp CPT.

**Quy trình:** Sinh viên co-op gặp cố vấn co-op của Steinbright trước. Sinh viên khác gặp cố vấn học thuật để xác nhận CPT là bắt buộc trong chương trình. records.question: OPT申请需要多长时间？
search_queries: OPT申请需要多长时间？
records.answer:
**OPT申请需要多长时间？**

OPT申请由美国公民及移民服务局（USCIS）审理，处理时间可能需要**90天或更长**。最新的处理时间可以在[USCIS案件处理时间页面](https://egov.uscis.gov/processing-times)查看（外部链接）。

**整个流程中的时间节点：**
- **ISSS签发OPT I-20：** 收到完整申请后约4-5个工作日。
- **向USCIS递交I-765：** 须在OPT建议日期起30天内提交。
- **收据通知（Receipt Notice）：** USCIS收到申请后约2-3周邮寄给您。
- 在拿到EAD（工作许可卡）之前不能开始工作。

**申请时间建议：**
- **毕业前OPT：** 最早可在希望开始日期前90天申请。若预计审理时间较长，可选择较早的开始日期。
- **毕业后OPT：** 最早可在项目结束日前90天申请，最晚是完成学业要求后60天内。建议尽早提交。如果USCIS在60天宽限期结束前未收到申请，申请会被拒绝，F-1身份也会终止。

**加急处理：** ISSS 2023年3月的公告提到，USCIS对部分OPT申请开放了I-907加急处理（费用1,500美元，30个日历日）。该公告较旧，费用和适用条件请向ISSS顾问确认。

另外，ISSS最新公告（2026年10月9日）提到DHS提议对OPT收取新费用，如需了解详情，请查看[该公告](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/October/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Proposes-$70000-Fee-for-OPT-and-$30000-fee-for-STEM-OPT)。

F-1 학생의 졸업 후 유예 기간(grace period)은 **60일**입니다. J-1 학생은 30일입니다. ([Maintaining F-1 and J-1 Student Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain))

- 출국 준비 및 짐 정리
- 미국 내 여행

**불가능한 것:** 근무 및 수학

**참고 사항:**
- OPT를 신청하거나 체류 자격 연장을 받지 않는 학생은 유예 기간 안에 출국해야 합니다. 유예 기간이 끝나기 전에 출국하면 I-20 만료일 이후에는 F-1 신분으로 재입국할 수 없습니다.
- OPT를 하는 경우, OPT EAD 카드가 만료된 후 60일의 유예 기간이 주어집니다. 단, OPT를 끝까지 마친 학생에게만 적용되며, 실업 기간 한도(OPT 90일, STEM OPT 150일)를 초과한 학생은 유예 기간을 받을 수 없습니다. records.question: Preciso de uma assinatura de viagem no meu I-20 para voltar aos EUA?
search_queries: Preciso de uma assinatura de viagem no meu I-20 para voltar aos EUA?
records.answer:
Sim. Para voltar aos EUA, o I-20 (F-1) precisa ter uma assinatura de viagem recente. Os prazos variam conforme a fonte:

- **Regra geral (página de Viagens):** assinatura emitida há no máximo **12 meses** da data de reentrada.
- **F-1 em OPT pós-conclusão ou STEM OPT:** no máximo **6 meses**.
- **Página de Renovação de Visto:** pede uma nova assinatura se a atual tiver mais de **6 meses** na data de retorno. Como é o prazo mais curto, ele é a escolha mais segura. Vale confirmar com a ISSS.

**Como solicitar:** use o [formulário de Signature Request](https://drexel.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KHlTvO1gmy8Sfs), indicado em um aviso da ISSS de dezembro de 2024.

**Outros documentos para levar na viagem (F-1):** passaporte válido por mais de seis meses após a data de retorno, visto F-1 válido, comprovante de pagamento da taxa SEVIS e, opcionalmente, histórico ou comprovante de matrícula. Se estiver em OPT/STEM, leve também o EAD válido e, opcionalmente, comprovante de emprego.

A ISSS também pede que você consulte o escritório antes de fazer planos de viagem ou sair dos EUA, pois podem ocorrer mudanças repentinas nas regras de imigração. Isso consta em um aviso de fevereiro de 2025, portanto confirme com um consultor da ISSS se ainda vale.

records.question: Do I pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again after a long leave?
search_queries: Do I pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again after a long leave?
records.answer:
It depends on how long you're away and what happens to your SEVIS record.

**You must repay the SEVIS I-901 fee** if you need a new I-20/DS-2019. That applies when:
- you have not been enrolled for **more than five (5) months**, or
- your SEVIS record was terminated for reasons other than "Authorized Early Withdrawal."

**Shorter authorized absences (under 5 months):** You can ask ISSS to reactivate your SEVIS record instead. The page doesn't mention a new fee for reactivation. Be aware that SEVP decides whether to approve it. If SEVP denies it, you'll need a new I-20, which means repaying the fee.

**Key steps for a long absence:**
- Email ISSS at least **3 months** before your planned return to get instructions for applying for a new I-20/DS-2019.
- Because this causes a break in F-1 status, you must complete at least one academic year of full-time study after returning before you're eligible for certain F-1 benefits, such as CPT or OPT.
- You also need approval from your academic program to return from leave. Your academic advisor can tell you how to report your return.

You can pay the fee at [FMJfee.com](https://fmjfee.com/i901fee/index.html), the site ISSS lists for initial F-1/J-1 students. For your specific situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: 212(e) two-year home country requirement
search_queries: 212(e) two-year home country requirement
records.answer:
**What it is:** Some J-1 exchange visitors can't become lawful permanent residents or change to another visa status in the U.S. until they have lived and been physically present in their country of nationality or last legal permanent residence for a total of at least two years after leaving the U.S. in J-1 status.

**Who it applies to:**
- Those whose program was financed, directly or indirectly, in whole or part, by a U.S. government agency or by the government of their home country (or last country of residence).
- Those who were nationals or residents of a country that the U.S. Department of State has designated as needing people with their specialized field of knowledge or skill. ISSS says students pursuing a major on their home country's skills list are deemed subject to it.

**Waiver:**
- You may be able to apply for a waiver, but ISSS may not assist with J-1 waivers, because the Department of State sees this as a conflict of interest for J-1 sponsors. See the [Department of State's waiver instructions](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/study/exchange/waiver-of-the-exchange-visitor.html) (external).
- Waiver cases can take a year or longer, and applying or receiving a waiver doesn't automatically extend your legal stay.
- After a favorable recommendation, you lose eligibility for J-1 extension, J-1 transfer, and a new J-1 visa.

**H-1B impact:** If you're subject to 212(e), you can't begin H-1B employment until you've received a waiver of 212(e) ([H-1B FAQ](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/hiring-foreign-nationals/h1b-temp/h1b-faq)).

records.question: H-1B cap-gap extension
search_queries: H-1B cap-gap extension
records.answer:
**H-1B cap-gap** is the period between the end of your OPT (or STEM OPT) and the start of your H-1B status. If you filed a timely change of status to H-1B with an October 1 start date, your work authorization is automatically extended while that application is pending, through October 1 or until it is approved.

**You're eligible if:**
- Your employer files the H-1B petition on or after April 1 and requests a change of status starting October 1.
- You are still within your OPT/STEM OPT authorization period when the petition is submitted.

**To get a cap-gap I-20:**
1. Email ISSS to confirm your employment and address information in SEVIS is accurate (errors will significantly delay the I-20).
2. Email ISSS one of these:
   - For cap-gap through June 1: an employer statement that the change of status was properly filed, plus proof of delivery to USCIS.
   - For cap-gap beyond June 1: a scanned USCIS receipt or proof the petition was wait-listed.

ISSS will email you when the new I-20 is ready.

**Other points:**
- If the petition is denied, rejected, or revoked and your EAD is still valid, work permission ends on the EAD end date. If your OPT has already expired, it ends on the rejection, denial, revocation, or withdrawal date.
- The unemployment limit continues during cap-gap.
- A January 2025 announcement says the H-1B Modernization Rule extends cap-gap protection to as late as April 1 of the following year. The OPT and STEM OPT pages still describe the October 1 timing, so please confirm with an ISSS advisor which applies to you.
- Check with your employer or immigration attorney before traveling abroad during cap-gap.

**Timing for applying for STEM OPT:**

- **Earliest:** You may file up to 90 days before your Post-Completion OPT end date.
- **Send ISSS your documents** no later than 30 days before your current OPT EAD end date, to allow time for processing and mailing.
- **Hard deadline:** USCIS must receive your application before your OPT EAD card expires. If it doesn't, you won't be eligible for the extension.
- **60-day window:** USCIS must also receive your application within 60 days of the date ISSS prints your STEM OPT Request I-20. Otherwise you'll need to redo the application.

**If your EAD expires while your application is pending:** If you applied on time, you may keep working up to 180 days past the expiration date while the application is pending, with your valid I-797 receipt notice.

**Other notes:**
- You must be in the U.S. to apply. If you're abroad and can't return, email ISSS.
- If you get an RFE or your I-765 is rejected or returned, contact ISSS immediately.

Because these deadlines are strict, please confirm your specific dates with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Can I travel abroad while it's pending?
history: How long does it take USCIS to approve it?
search_queries: Can I travel abroad while OPT application is pending?
Can I travel abroad while it's pending? | How long does it take USCIS to approve it? | What is OPT?
records.answer:
It depends on which type of OPT you've applied for.

**Initial OPT (pending):**
- **Pre-Completion OPT:** You may travel and re-enter under the general F-1 travel requirements.
- **Post-Completion OPT, before you finish your degree:** If you're returning to resume your studies, the general F-1 travel requirements apply.
- **Post-Completion OPT, after you finish your degree (during the 60-day grace period):** ISSS says travel before approval "may be slightly risky." The F-1 regulations don't directly address it, but most students have re-entered successfully with a copy of the USCIS OPT Receipt Notice. Carry:
  - Valid passport
  - Valid F-1 visa (Canada and Bermuda citizens are exempt)
  - I-20 with the OPT recommendation and a travel signature no older than 6 months
  - OPT Receipt Notice (mailed 2-3 weeks after USCIS receives your application)

**STEM OPT (pending):**
- If your current OPT has **not expired** when you re-enter, you should be able to return.
- If it **has expired**, travel may be risky, and ISSS can't guarantee entry, since Customs and Border Protection makes the decision.
- Carry the same documents, plus your expired OPT EAD and a letter from your STEM employer (job title, description, start/end dates, salary).

Also, ISSS reported on January 8, 2026 that USCIS placed a hold on pending applications, including OPT and STEM OPT, for people from certain travel-ban countries. If that may apply to you, contact ISSS.

Because the risk depends on your situation, please confirm your plans with an ISSS advisor before traveling.

records.question: What do I need to do before I come back?
history: I want to take a term off and go home next quarter.
search_queries: requirements before returning from term off vacation break
What do I need to do before I come back? | I want to take a term off and go home next quarter.
records.answer:
What you need to do depends on how long you're away and how your SEVIS record was handled.

**First, for any return:** get approval from your academic program. Contact your academic advisor for instructions on reporting your return to Drexel.

**Absence authorized by ISSS and under 5 months:** you can request SEVIS reactivation. Submit these at least 1-2 months before you return:
- I-94 travel history, as proof you left the U.S.
- A copy of your flight itinerary showing your planned re-entry date
- Proof of full-time enrollment for the upcoming term (registration records or a letter from your academic advisor)

This is subject to SEVP discretion. If SEVP doesn't approve it, you'll need a new I-20 instead.

**Absence of more than 5 months, or SEVIS terminated for reasons other than "Authorized Early Withdrawal":** you need a new I-20/DS-2019 and must repay the SEVIS I-901 fee. Email ISSS at least 3 months before your planned return for instructions. This creates a break in F-1 status, so you must complete at least one academic year of full-time study before becoming eligible for benefits like CPT or OPT.

**Before you travel back**, ISSS's re-entry advisory lists these items:
- A passport valid at least 6 months beyond your return date
- A valid F-1/J-1 visa
- A recent travel signature on your I-20/DS-2019 (use the [Signature Request form](https://drexel.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KHlTvO1gmy8Sfs))
- Proof of enrollment

If you need a new visa, contact ISSS before leaving the U.S. Immigration rules can change quickly, so confirm your plan with an ISSS advisor (contact details on the [ISSS website](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support)).

Who is eligible for it? | What is Academic Training for J-1 students?
records.answer:
J-1 students who want Academic Training (AT) through Drexel must meet all of these requirements:

- Your DS-2019 was issued by Drexel University, not an outside agency (such as Fulbright).
- You are primarily in the U.S. to study, rather than to do academic training.
- You are in good academic standing.
- The training is directly related to the major field of study listed on your DS-2019.
- AT is approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date.
- AT starts no later than 30 days after your program ends.

**Time limits that affect eligibility:**
- Bachelor's and master's students: up to 18 months, or the length of the degree program if shorter (STEM degree students may qualify for a special extension).
- PhD students: up to 36 months, or the length of the degree program if shorter.
- Non-degree students: the DS-2019 cannot extend beyond 24 months in total, including degree completion and AT.

**Upcoming rule change:** The ISSS pages I found mention a DHS final rule on duration of status, scheduled to take effect September 15, 2026. An older 2025 proposal said J-1 students would need to apply to USCIS for an extension to do post-graduation AT. However, the newest announcement (September 14, 2026) says a U.S. District Court postponed the rule's effective date. I couldn't find details of how AT would be affected in the excerpts, so please check the [announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status) and confirm with an ISSS advisor.

To check whether you personally qualify, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Tôi được phép thất nghiệp bao nhiêu ngày?

Tôi được phép thất nghiệp bao nhiêu ngày? | Tôi đang làm OPT sau khi tốt nghiệp.
records.answer:
**Trả lời ngắn:** Tối đa **90 ngày** thất nghiệp trong thời gian Post-Completion OPT (12 tháng đầu). Nếu sau đó bạn được duyệt gia hạn STEM OPT 24 tháng, bạn được thêm **60 ngày**, tổng cộng tối đa **150 ngày**.

**Cách tính:**
- Mỗi ngày (kể cả cuối tuần) bạn không có việc làm hợp lệ, kể từ ngày bắt đầu việc làm ghi trên thẻ EAD, đều được tính là một ngày thất nghiệp.
- Làm việc từ xa được phép, nhưng phải làm ít nhất 20 giờ mỗi tuần khi đang ở Post-Completion OPT.

**Cần làm:**
- Báo cáo việc làm cho ISSS và báo ngay nếu bạn bị gián đoạn hoặc mất việc.
- Nếu sắp hết giới hạn, bạn phải thực hiện một trong các hành động sau **trước** ngày thất nghiệp cuối cùng: nộp đơn chuyển bậc học hoặc chuyển trường SEVP-certified, rời khỏi Hoa Kỳ, hoặc có biện pháp khác để duy trì tình trạng hợp pháp. Nếu không, bạn vi phạm tình trạng F-1.
- Nếu đang ở STEM OPT và mất việc hoặc nghỉ việc trước khi kỳ STEM OPT kết thúc, bạn phải báo ISSS và nộp bản đánh giá cuối cùng trên Form I-983 trong vòng 10 ngày.

Vì tình huống của mỗi người khác nhau, hãy xác nhận với cố vấn ISSS về số ngày thất nghiệp còn lại của bạn.
